decisions.why: FR-010 and amendment 1 ('Refuse writes to the tree while your own gate runs'); each refused write moves HEAD or a tracked file that preflight.py --tree-check hashes, so each voids the gate - enforcement of what was asked.

decisions.summary: git add is let through while the gate runs, on the premise that it moves nothing the gate checks
decisions.why: The premise is false, measured 2026-10-17 by this reviewer: preflight.py tree() keys on `git diff --name-only HEAD`, and in a scratch repo `git add` of an untracked file made it appear in that list (before: empty; after: 'new'), so tree_moved() reports it and the gate goes NOT GREEN. Staging a new file is the ordinary step before a commit, so the carve-out passes exactly the gate-voiding write FR-010 exists to stop (purpose-fatal). The earlier CLEAR text refused git add. Fix: refuse a git add that stages any path not already in `git diff --name-only HEAD` (a new file), or refuse git add whole; a git add of an already-modified tracked file may pass.

decisions.summary: make record-checked and make modal-triaged are let through as writing only under .git/
decisions.why: Adjudicated per target. modal-triaged: within - modal_triage.py record writes the store and its TOUCHED mark only, under .git/. record-checked: the premise is false for one of its forms - with REPLY= it runs record_owed.file_outside(), which appends to the active feature's specs/<NNN>/found.jsonl, a TRACKED file (git ls-files lists specs/335-.../found.jsonl and others), so it moves the tracked tree and voids the gate. (REASON= writes a new untracked file under dev/bypass-log/, which tree() does not see.) Fix: refuse make record-checked when REPLY= is given (or move found.jsonl writes to wait), and state the premise per form rather than for the target.

decisions.summary: Seed 40: dump first, then a row farm may take its own street's join as its street, in lay_door_paths and row_rules through one predicate. A re-seat, if one is needed, goes to T04.
decisions.why: This refines an O definition, which is the 'refine the number/rule' exit the GM's checklist names. Leaving homesteads unmoved is the GM's 'homesteads before lanes' (A5). The T04 route is ruled under D22-exit.

decisions.summary: Seed 21, exit (1): where a fouled way is a household's only route and it crosses a neighbor's yard, the household is reached across its neighbor (0246's fallback, R), but 'the way is not drawn through the yard, and the house counts as reached, as unreached_houses already allows.'
decisions.why: In amendment 1 the GM asked: 'Are we sure that household paths don't cut through neighbors' yards? I thought that our research findings were that they did.' The R label the plan carries attaches only to 'reached across a neighbor's yard'. The clause 'the way is not drawn through the yard' has no research basis in the plan. Its only stated ground is existing code (unreached_houses), and preserving existing behavior the GM did not ask to preserve does not make an exception legitimate. Here that behavior is the one the GM's question challenged: no path through a neighbor's yard. The blind block does not carry the clause ('0246's own fallback is reaching the house across a neighbor's yard'). The Decisions preface says that where block and session differ on seeds 17 and 21 'the decision names the measurement that settles it, not a side'. D20(1) takes a side and names no measurement, and FR-012 requires the plan to say where it differs from the blind block. It should say one of two things instead. (a) The household's way is drawn across the neighbor's yard, as an exception to fouled_segment for that case. Or (b) the decision quotes the 0246 line showing that such a crossing leaves no drawn path, labels 'not drawn' R on that line, and marks it as the session's difference from the blind block.

decisions.summary: Seed 21, exit (2): otherwise the 7 ft O gap is weighed against more room, room first under the GM's 2026-10-12 ruling, and a room change goes to T04. Before choosing, the session asks whether a reader of the research would call the drawn place wrong.
decisions.why: Room first is the GM's ruling and 'give it more room' is a checklist exit. The reader question is the GM's 'say that there isn't a problem' from amendment 1. The T04 route is ruled under D22-exit.

decisions.summary: Seed 17: per-candidate refusal first, then D17's merge, then 0014's nearest lane run on to the bund, then whether the refusal should exist at all. FIELD_REACH_FT's 60 ft is relabeled O.
decisions.why: Exit (3) keeps the GM's own question open ('I didn't think that there was a rule about village lanes needing to reach the fields'). Relabeling the mislabeled figure is constitution XIV. Every exit resolves inside T03.

decisions.summary: Done: 'each seed passes make cohort N=1 SEED=n, or carries its recorded exit'. With D19 and D20(2), a seed whose exit is a re-seat or a room change leaves T03 for T04.
decisions.why: FR-007 moves the four seeds here as a unit, and this lets one leave T03 still failing. The GM's own words imply the exception: 'Nobody in real life moves their house so that a footpath will join'. Homesteads come before lanes, so a lane task may not re-seat houses. The approved scope order puts T48 (the web carries a re-deal of the seats) directly after the seeds. Every deferral the decisions name goes to T04, a task in this feature. This is legitimate ONLY as that T04 deferral. A seed left with a 'recorded exit' that no task in this feature owns, or an exit other than a re-seat or room change, is not covered by this ruling.

decisions.summary: Done also includes: the 50/54 baseline log, no regression across the cohort, the merge test red without its change, the Inashiro glyph-check re-run with F1-F3 gone, make done green, and a retro row.
decisions.why: Each item enforces what was asked (FR-007's seeds and lane law, FR-006's retro). It is enforcement, not unrequested scope.

It is left to the page that owns it, and the GM did not ask for it to change. 4. The dump (D16) is named as the measurement that decides whether the case applies, as the Decisions preface requires. 5. The difference from the blind block is marked, as FR-012 asks. Caveat: the bundle does not carry 0246's page or the 2026-10-03 ruling, so the two quotes were not checked against their sources. This ruling holds only if they are quoted accurately. decisions.summary: The side-by-side merge becomes its own settle step (settle_side_by_side), run after the reach and before the network rule, that never refuses; REACH 20 ft for the merge only.
decisions.why: The GM's request names merging near-parallel close paths as 'adding a rule ... where the new rule did in fact solve the problem'; the approved proposal: 'Add a rule that removes the case, like merging two near-parallel paths'. A step that only adds merges is that rule. Moving REACH out of the refusal (part B 3, 5) stops tuning one number, which is the thrashing the request exists to end.

decisions.summary: A merge cut is written only where the cut way keeps the law (Lawful); otherwise the pair is left unmerged.
decisions.why: An 'only where' on the requested merge, so ruled as an exception, each residue case separately. (a) An unmendable pair within 14 ft is refused by the doubled-tail rule, exactly as before T03. (b) An unmendable pair at 14-20 ft is drawn as two ways, exactly as before T03. Neither case is worse than HEAD; the condition only declines to add a merge that would break the lane law. It is implied by the GM's own words: 'I don't want future sessions to just throw away rules when they are inconvenient', and the approved guardrail that loosening a rule needs its reason recorded - an unlawful cut would drop the law with no record. The bundle cannot show what Lawful contains: a merge T meets its partner within _DOUBLED_DEG of parallel, and if Lawful's meeting-angle rule vetoes such a T the step would be hollow and the exception purpose-fatal. The ruling therefore rests on D22's backstops, which fail if that happens: the merge test red first on Inashiro lanes 8 and 14 and seed 49's root way, and the Inashiro glyph-check re-run with F1-F3 gone. If either is met by narrowing them rather than by merges, this ruling does not hold.

decisions.summary: The lane law's doubled-tail rule keeps _ALONG_FT 14 ft as a refusal; the law is not widened.
decisions.why: Classified on this review's reading, not the plan's label. The refusal reaches only pairs the merge could not mend, so it narrows nothing the merge does; the number is O (part B 2), a knob left where T01 put it. The GM did not ask that refusal removed, and widening it to 20 ft is what refused household ways and a farmhouse (part B 1).

decisions.summary: T01's three detectors are kept as they are (earlier: each retired where the general test covers its cases).
decisions.why: Retirement was cleanup, not a requested behavior; keeping refusal detectors behind a merge that runs first narrows nothing asked. Design, not fidelity.

decisions.summary: The red-first merge test is now Inashiro lanes 8 and 14 and seed 49's root way; F2's pairs are no longer in it (earlier text named them).
decisions.why: F2 is still owed twice: D17 still measures F2's 18-25 ft pairs against REACH and moves REACH rather than keep F2, and D22 still requires the Inashiro glyph-check re-run with F1-F3 gone. With both standing, dropping F2 from the red-first list changes which test proves the merge, not what is asked.

decisions.summary: Seed 49, found failing at HEAD in the 60-seed cohort, is fixed (own-garden change plus D17's merge) and held by D22's cohort with the four.
decisions.why: The request names four seeds, so a fifth would be scope if it carried new work; it does not. Both its causes are covered by work already in scope (the own-garden change made for seed 21, and the requested merge, since its root way ran 18 ft beside the skeleton), so it serves as a test case of the requested behavior. Note: D22's baseline line still lists only 17, 21, 40 and 45.

decisions.summary: The 7 ft fence gap does not apply along a household's own garden (Approach 3: O, a DEVIATION on 0246's drawing page; D24 relies on it).
decisions.why: Found in prose: it is relied on in the Approach and D24 but decided in none of the changed blocks; D20 is unchanged and its listed exits do not name it. It loosens our own convention (the 7 ft gap is labeled O), through D20(2)'s weighing of that gap, with the reason recorded as a DEVIATION - the exit ('add a principled exception') and the guardrail the GM's approved proposal names. It narrows nothing the GM asked. The caller should confirm an unchanged block (or D20, amended) records the decision itself; a plan relying on a decision no Decisions entry carries is the gap MODE 4 exists for, even where the decision is sound.

decisions.summary: D17's side-by-side merge (with seed 49 / D24 and seed 55) leaves T03 and is carried to T12 (part B 22:20 item 5, Approach 22:23 items 1, 2 and 6, D25); D22's merge-test, F1-F3 glyph-check and exit-to-T04 lines are read per D25 as owned by T12.
decisions.why: The merge is the GM's own principle ("a single footpath would emerge") and the approved proposal placed it in the lane-law task; it was already moved to T03 under earlier CLEAR verdicts, and the amendment-1 text described T03 as 'the four seeds plus the general side-by-side merge', so taking it out of T03 narrows T03. It is deferred, not removed: it stays inside this feature, owned by T12 (whose existence I can see only in the Landing block), with the cause of its failure diagnosed (the later settle passes do not see the junctions it makes). Two grounds make it legitimate. First, the request's stated purpose is to stop hyper-focusing on one thing and step back to ask whether there is a better approach, and a third tuning of REACH is the exact thrash the GM described. Second, the round arbiter, which stands where the GM was asked (feature 379), ruled change-route and then route (a) at hour 6. I took that ruling from the dispatch because the bundle forbids reading arbiter.jsonl. Condition: T03's retro row must count the hours spent on the merge attempt as T03's own, because per-task timing is what the feature exists to measure and carrying the work out makes T03 look shorter than it was.

The GM's request never names seed 57, so no clause of the request is lost. The residue is diagnosed (lanes 1/13, settle_knots' gather of lane 13 refused by needle_loops), was cut from 4 knots to 2 by bisection, is owned by T12, and was put back to the arbiter with the measurement and waived (ask:t03-seed57-residue, taken from the dispatch; I did not read the ruling). Because the arbiter stands in the GM's place, this is a decided exception and not one a session carved out for itself.

It follows a measurement (21:22: seed 21's ways come near only their own household's garden and yard), and it rejects 'more room' on a stated ground (the distance is to the household's own beds, not between homesteads), which honors the GM's room-first ruling. Whether the code site also carries the reason is for implementation review. D25 attributes seed 57's residue to this fix, and that link is ruled on in seed57-residue-waived.
